info.title: MGM described API
info.summary: The GUI host's routes, and the route of every action MGM's plugins describe.
info.description:
**Experimental while GUI_CONTRACT is 0.x.** `info.version` is GUI_CONTRACT, 0.2.1 here. It versions the shapes the GUI contract defines: what the host's routes take and answer, and how the catalog describes an action. Until 1.0 a minor version may change any of those shapes, and a patch only adds optional fields, kinds or values.

It does not version what the document lists. Actions, their routes and the codes they answer are added and changed from one MGM release to the next while GUI_CONTRACT stays the same, and an action's body is its own: each action gives the version of its input as `inputVersion`, under `x-mgm-actions`. Read the document of the MGM release you call.

MGM's API is the routes it already has: the GUI host's routes under /api/gui/, which describe MGM and read it, and the route of each action a plugin contributes, the only way to write. Each operation needs a signed-in person, and acts with what that person may do in a browser.

The GUI host's routes refuse with `{ error, code }` (HostFailureBody): read `code`, which is stable, and show `error`. An action's route answers the codes this document names for it in `code` too, but its own refusals were written before the described API and are not all alike (ActionRefusal says how to read them). Each operation names the codes its route is known to answer, in each response's `x-mgm-codes`, and `x-mgm-error-codes` lists them all with what each means. On an action's route that list is partial, and each response says so with `x-mgm-codes-complete: false`. Middleware answers two requests itself, before any route, and with no code: a request with no session (401, `{ error }`), and one to a path this release does not serve (404, plain text; such an operation says `x-mgm-released: false`).

An action's route is listed with its actions under `x-mgm-actions`, as GET /api/gui/catalog describes them; the catalog also says which the person may send now. An action is prepared with POST /api/gui/prepare, then sent to its own route.

Generated from MGM's action registry by `npm run api:openapi`; do not edit it by hand.

patch.description:
The route of 5 actions, listed under `x-mgm-actions` as the action catalog (GET /api/gui/catalog) describes each. Prepare an action first (POST /api/gui/prepare): it answers the confirmation step its route checks.

The answer to a write is the route's own and is not described here yet. Nor are the route's own refusals: each response names the codes this document knows the route answers, and says with `x-mgm-codes-complete: false` that there may be others (ActionRefusal).

parameters.name: lineItemId

400.description:
- `invalid_body`: The body is not JSON, or the action's input refuses it. `error` describes the first problem, and `field` names the top-level field it is in, when there is one.

And refusals of the route's own, which this document does not list yet.

401.description:
Middleware answers a request with no session `{ error }`, with no code, before the route runs.

The route's own, when Supabase Auth refuses a session middleware let through, such as one signed out on another device. Some routes answer it with a code, some with a `reason` or only text.

409.description:
- `billing_disabled`: The plugin is off for the organization the request targets. Its records are kept, and it is turned on in Settings → Plugins.

And refusals of the route's own, which this document does not list yet.

503.description:
- `billing_gate_unavailable`: Whether the plugin is on could not be read, so nothing was done. Try again.

And refusals of the route's own, which this document does not list yet.

default.description: Any other refusal: the route's own, at a status not described above.

get.summary: The actions the person may see, and whether each can be sent now
get.description:
Every action contributed to the organization, in catalog order and then by id, with its route, its input as JSON Schema and whether it is available, and why not. Reads only: it asks each action's own `available()`, but never prepares or sends one.

Takes `org`, or up to 4 `entity=<kind>:<id>`, each of another kind, and nothing else. Entities decide the organization and limit the list to the actions offered on their kinds. A person who reaches no organization but rents a unit, or whose roles are all tenant roles, gets no actions.

The organization the person last used (a cookie MGM sets) is a hint when the request names none; like `org`, it only chooses among the organizations the person can see.

This route is not part of this release: middleware answers every request to it 404, with a plain-text body and no code, before the route runs.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description: The organization to answer for. One the person cannot see is a 404.

parameters.name: entity
parameters.description: A record to ask about, as `<kind>:<id>`. Not together with `org`.

200.description: The actions, each with its availability.

400.description: - `gui_bad_request`: The query or the body breaks the route's rules: a parameter it does not take, one given twice or of the wrong form, or a body that is not JSON or not the request's shape.

401.description:
Middleware answers a request with no session `{ error }`, with no code, before the route runs.

- `gui_unauthenticated`: No signed-in person: Supabase Auth does not accept the session.

403.description: - `gui_no_access`: The person holds no role, or reaches no organization the answer needs.

404.description:
This route is not part of this release: middleware answers every request to it 404, with a plain-text body and no code, before the route runs.

- `gui_not_found`: Nothing the person can see answers the request: an unknown view or action, or a record they cannot see. It does not say whether such a record exists.

500.description: - `gui_output_invalid`: What the host built, or what a contribution returned, broke the contract's schema, so none of it is sent.

503.description: - `gui_unavailable`: Something the answer needs could not be read right now. Nothing was written; try again.

get.summary: The person's manifest: places, navigation and the views it names
get.description:
The manifest the signed-in layout renders, with the interface the installation serves. Takes `path` and `org`, each at most once, and nothing else.

The organization asked for is `org`, else the `?org=` of `path`. The organization the person last used (a cookie MGM sets) is a hint when the request names none; like `org`, it only chooses among the organizations the person can see.

This route is not part of this release: middleware answers every request to it 404, with a plain-text body and no code, before the route runs.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: A page on this site, with its own query: the manifest is built for it.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description: The organization to build the manifest for.

400.description: - `gui_bad_request`: The query or the body breaks the route's rules: a parameter it does not take, one given twice or of the wrong form, or a body that is not JSON or not the request's shape.

401.description:
Middleware answers a request with no session `{ error }`, with no code, before the route runs.

- `gui_unauthenticated`: No signed-in person: Supabase Auth does not accept the session.

403.description: - `gui_no_access`: The person holds no role, or reaches no organization the answer needs.

404.description: This route is not part of this release: middleware answers every request to it 404, with a plain-text body and no code, before the route runs.

500.description: - `gui_manifest_failed`: The manifest could not be built, also when MGM_GUI names no interface this build serves.

post.summary: An action's form and confirmation step
post.description:
Prepares one action on its records for the signed-in person: the JSON Schema of the fields a person enters, a cleaned prefill, the confirmation step and the route and method the write goes to. Writes nothing: the write is sent to the action's own route, which checks the confirmation again.

The body is read up to 16384 bytes.

400.description: - `gui_bad_request`: The query or the body breaks the route's rules: a parameter it does not take, one given twice or of the wrong form, or a body that is not JSON or not the request's shape.

401.description:
Middleware answers a request with no session `{ error }`, with no code, before the route runs.

- `gui_unauthenticated`: No signed-in person: Supabase Auth does not accept the session.

403.description:
- `gui_action_refused`: The action's own prepare refused it, for a reason other than not finding its record. The status and the message are the action's.
- `gui_human_only`: The action is human-only, and it was asked for as a proposal (with `provenance`).
- `gui_no_access`: The person holds no role, or reaches no organization the answer needs.

404.description: - `gui_not_found`: Nothing the person can see answers the request: an unknown view or action, or a record they cannot see. It does not say whether such a record exists.

409.description:
- `billing_disabled`: The plugin is off for the organization the request targets. Its records are kept, and it is turned on in Settings → Plugins.
- `gui_action_refused`: The action's own prepare refused it, for a reason other than not finding its record. The status and the message are the action's.
- `gui_action_unavailable`: The action's own available() said no for this record; the message says why.

413.description: - `gui_body_too_large`: The request body is larger than the route reads.

500.description:
- `gui_action_refused`: The action's own prepare refused it, for a reason other than not finding its record. The status and the message are the action's.
- `gui_output_invalid`: What the host built, or what a contribution returned, broke the contract's schema, so none of it is sent.
- `gui_prepare_failed`: The action's own prepare threw.

503.description:
- `billing_gate_unavailable`: Whether the plugin is on could not be read, so nothing was done. Try again.
- `gui_action_refused`: The action's own prepare refused it, for a reason other than not finding its record. The status and the message are the action's.
- `gui_unavailable`: Something the answer needs could not be read right now. Nothing was written; try again.
- `payments_gate_unavailable`: Whether the plugin is on could not be read, so nothing was done. Try again.

ActionRefusal.description:
How an action's route refuses. A code this document names for the route comes in `code`, which is stable. The route's own refusals were written before the described API and are not all alike: one may carry `code`, a `reason` instead, or only text. The text to show a person is `error`, or `message` where there is no `error`.

Read it as MGM's GUI kit does: `code` when there is one, and `error`, else `message`. A route may add fields of its own, such as `field`, the body field a problem is in.
